# Digital Asset Links

`assetlinks.json` is what tells Android that the app signed with a particular
key is allowed to open safestart.trust-raise.com without an address bar. If a
fingerprint here does not match the key the installed app was signed with, the
app still works but shows a Chrome address bar across the top, which looks
broken and is the single most common Trusted Web Activity mistake.

## Both fingerprints are in, as of 22 September 2026

**The upload key**, generated by PWABuilder when it built the package:

    42:84:B7:92:...:D1:C7

That key lives in `signing.keystore`, in the PWABuilder download, and it is not
in this repo and must never be. `.gitignore` covers `*.keystore`, `*.jks` and
`*.p12`, but the real protection is keeping it somewhere else entirely. Lose it
and SafeStart can never be updated under this listing again.

**Play's app signing key**, read from Play Console after the first upload:

    50:A8:91:33:...:43:D8

Why two. Play strips the upload signature and re-signs every release with a key
Google holds, so the signature that reaches a parent's phone is Google's and not
ours. Listing only the upload key is the failure that looks like success: the
app is perfect on the machine that built it and shows an address bar on every
phone that installed it from the store.

`check.js` now fails the build if either one goes missing, if a fingerprint is
malformed, or if the same one is listed twice.

## Where to find Play's key again

Play Console renames this section regularly. As of September 2026:

    Protected with Play → Play Store protection → Play app signing

Then the **App signing key** section, not the **Upload key** section.

## Checking it worked

This has to be readable at exactly:

    https://safestart.trust-raise.com/.well-known/assetlinks.json

served as `application/json`, which `vercel.json` already handles. Google's own
checker:

    https://developers.google.com/digital-asset-links/tools/generator

The real test is installing the build Play distributes, not the one built here,
and looking at the top of the screen.
